Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with logical sections (Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Results, Discussion, Conclusion) and clearly articulates the core idea of reading uncertainty signals from intermediate logit-lens distributions before final-layer calibration. Technical components such as the degeneracy screen, per-model selection, and protocol-internal validity anchor (A2-v2) are explained with explicit equations, algorithms, and figures. Minor deductions for extreme length and density of protocol details that occasionally obscure the main narrative flow.

Novelty.justification: The work introduces the first AUROC evaluation of raw per-layer logit-lens statistics (entropy, max-probability, adjacent-layer KL) as training-free, sampling-free hallucination detectors with per-model layer selection. Adjacent-layer KL is newly positioned as a detection score (previously only a decoding heuristic). The methodological contribution of protocol-internal validity anchoring, motivated by a quantitative provenance audit showing six protocol differences shifting AUROC by +0.074, is original.

Soundness.justification: Methods are appropriate and reproducible: three 7-8B models, two QA datasets, greedy generation + teacher-forced re-forward, degeneracy screening retaining 15-20 layers per cell, corrected AUROC with direction selection, and within-sweep final-layer baselines. All reported numbers match the provided code outputs and experiment logs. No major experimental flaws; limitations (selection-split point estimates only, single seed, no CIs) are explicitly stated and the staged design defers test-split evaluation.

Significance.justification: The paper addresses a practically important problem—cheap, training-free hallucination detection for open-weight LLMs—showing a universal point-estimate depth advantage (L28-L31 band) across all six model×dataset cells (AUROC 0.6092–0.7011 vs. 0.55 gate). However, all results are selection-split only, the largest depth margin on one cell is within plausible noise (+0.0035), and scope is narrow (three families, two short-form QA datasets). Impact is incremental rather than transformative.

strengths: Rigorous, reproducible protocol with identity-verified cache reuse, within-sweep baselines, and explicit staged verification design
Consistent existence of class-separable intermediate-layer signals and depth advantage in every cell, supported by matching code and figures
weaknesses: All quantitative claims are selection-split point estimates; locked test splits were never evaluated and no confidence intervals are reported
Narrow scope and modest margins in several cells limit immediate generalizability and practical deployment claims
